$why: WHAT THIS FILE IS. The set of leagues this product covers, and the tier of every league Riot
returns. It is a PRODUCT DECISION, not a transcription of anything upstream. The owner decided
on 2026-08-11 that phase one covers three international events (Worlds, MSI, First Stand) and
five regional leagues (LCK, LPL, LEC, LCS, LCP). Everything else Riot returns is marked minor.
WHY IT IS A FILE AND NOT CODE. There is no machine-readable tier signal in Riot's API and there
cannot be one derived from it: getLeagues.priority is 1 for all 45 leagues, and displayPriority
is per-request UI state rather than a league property. Both verified exhaustively over the
2026-08-09 capture of getLeagues -- see docs/sources/lolesports-rest.md. So coverage has to be
stated somewhere, and it belongs in configuration that changes on a product decision.
An earlier version of this file justified its contents by an observation of the lolesports.com
league picker. That justification is withdrawn: it was a single unrepeatable human observation
with no artifact, and it was never needed. The scope of this product does not require evidence
about Riot's website -- it requires a decision by the owner, which is what is recorded above.
TIER GATES TWO THINGS, AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME SET.
(a) Which matches have their teams resolved at all -- gated on the tier of the league the
match is played under. All eight major slugs qualify, international events included: a
Worlds match must resolve T1.
(b) Which leagues contribute rows to the team master table -- only majors with kind 'region'.
International events must NOT contribute. getTeams homes seven active rows at Worlds and
MSI, and none of them is a team that plays: five are 2011-era orgs (EPIK Gamer, Team
GAMED.DE, against All authority, Pacific eSports, Xan) and two are region placeholder
entities literally named 'LCS' and 'VCS' carrying those codes. Measured over the full
1568-row getTeams capture of 2026-08-09.
This distinction was invisible while all fourteen majors were regional leagues. Narrowing
to eight exposed it. That is why `kind` is required on every major entry.
MEASURED under the eight-major table, against the full 1568-row getTeams capture (1176 active):
- team index, regional majors only: 168 rows. By NAME: 168 distinct, ZERO collisions. By CODE:
167 distinct, one collision (EG). Since 2026-08-11 the join key is NAME and code is only a
fallback, because a code names the ORGANISATION rather than the squad: all seven LCK orgs
with an academy team share a code across the pair and share no name. A code join therefore
resolved an academy side to its parent and needed the tier gate to be safe; a name join does
not. See src/sources/riot/rest/teams.ts and docs/sources/lolesports-rest.md.
- including the international majors would add the seven junk rows described above and take
the index to 175 -- no new collision today, but two of those codes are LCS and VCS.
- over fixtures/riot-lol/rest_getSchedule.json: 60 of 160 sides resolve, 0 unresolved, 0
ambiguous, 100 out of scope.
Resolution is additionally gated on (a). That gate used to be the SAFETY mechanism -- without it,
a code join handed eleven sides in rest_getSchedule.json the wrong LCK org's id, and a wrong
identity is worse than an absent one. The name join removed that hazard, so the gate is now a
SCOPE decision: do not spend a lookup on a league we do not cover.
AN EXPLICIT 'minor' AND AN ABSENT SLUG ARE DIFFERENT STATES. Absent means a league appeared
upstream after this file was last touched: it resolves to 'unclassified' and warns. Three
leagues appeared during 2026 (ewc_lol, cacg, fls -- known from the season restructure, not
measurable from a single-day capture), so that path is load-bearing.

teamOverrides.reason: Evil Geniuses LG (LCS). A FALLBACK, not the primary mechanism, since 2026-08-11: the join is by name now, and getTeams names these two orgs distinctly ('Evil Geniuses LG' vs 'Evil Geniuses EU'), so if getSchedule uses the same names this override never fires. It is retained because EG appears in NEITHER committed schedule capture, so whether getSchedule writes the full name or a bare 'Evil Geniuses' is unverified. If it writes the bare name, the name lookup misses, the code lookup finds two rows, and this settles it. Delete only after a capture proves it unnecessary.
